text: Went at seven in the evening, which is when it actually looks like something. The plaza is wide enough that the pram was no trouble at all with my mother. Get there before six if you want a photograph without forty people in it.
Fine, but there is not much to do once you are standing under it. Twenty minutes is about right. No toilets anywhere near, which we found out the hard way with a small child.
Flat the whole way from the road, benches on the sea side, and the kids could run about without us chasing them. Empty before ten which was the best part.

The children lasted about forty minutes before they were done, and it is far too formal to let them run around. Our mistake. The food was excellent and the bill was as advertised as painful.

text: Tried to push a stroller down the main lane and gave up halfway. Steps, cables, broken paving, and no room to pass anyone. The baby was in a carrier and it was still miserable.
Came just to walk and look. There are still a couple of old tailoring shops and a book stall that have survived. Go on a weekday, it is a completely different street at four on a Tuesday.
We are both over seventy and the courtyard at the back is flat with tables in the shade. It is the only coffee stop in Colaba we could sit in comfortably. Waiters are used to older people.
I work from the courtyard two afternoons a week. Nobody rushes you, the coffee is good, and the front room gets unpleasantly loud after two.
Fine coffee, tiny room, and we were crammed into a table meant for two with four of us. The courtyard was taken. Book nothing, just go early.
The filter coffee is the best in the area and I have been coming for years. Worth knowing the South Indian room is up a narrow staircase with a turn, so I take my coffee downstairs now.
Food is good, the room is not. Carrying a one year old up that staircase while holding a cup of coffee is a bad afternoon. The art room downstairs saved us.
Turned up on a Monday after walking from the Taj and it was shut. Nobody had told us anywhere. Do not plan around this without checking the day.
Exactly what I needed between two meetings. Bagel in, fifteen minutes, out. Small room so it is no good for a group but perfect if you are on your own and short of time.
The kids eat bagels, we eat bagels, everyone is happy in fifteen minutes flat. That is the whole appeal when you have a two year window and a toddler in tow.
The menu runs all day which is why it works when everything else has shut. Nothing special, and that is the point at one o clock.
Good sandwiches, cramped seating, and the pavement noise is constant because the window is on the road. Fine for lunch, not for an evening.
My parents have eaten here for forty years and I finally understand the fuss. Level from the street, chairs with arms, and the berry pulao is worth the money.
Went late on a Saturday and it was deafening. Fantastic food, zero conversation possible after eight. Go at four.
Lovely food, but the room is dark, formal and full of adults talking. Our four year old lasted twenty minutes. Fine for us, wrong for us in the evening.

The only place I know in Colaba that will take eight of us at one in the morning without a booking. That is worth something. The food is broad, the noise is enormous, and it is not local in any sense.
We came for a drink, ended up staying until close. Not romantic, not special, but reliably open and the terrace is out of the wind.
We were in Mumbai for four days and it rained on three of them. The verandah here is why we were never stuck. My mother could sit under the roof and still be outside.
Good verandah, ordinary food, and it gets very tight after eight. We had to wait twenty minutes for a table we had not booked.
Hot chocolate and a window bench and we were happy for half an hour. It is not a destination, it is a very good gap in an afternoon.
Queue out the door on a Sunday and only four tables. We gave up and went next door. Worth trying on a weekday.
You are not going in, you are buying a drink and sitting on the terrace, and that is the whole arrangement. The building and the lawn are worth the money and the sea breeze is the best in Colaba.
Went to look at the building and we were politely turned away, which is fair enough. The lawn you can see from outside is nicer than most things anyway.
The terrace is level, there are chairs with arms, and the staff carried my mother tea. We would have been happy for the afternoon.
Five stops in seventy-five minutes, one frame each, and the man actually explained why the light was doing that. I have done walking tours that gave me less than this.

Twenty-four people, one tabla, and a singer who does not need a microphone. I have been to a hundred performances and I am still thinking about this one. Book a week out.

Two steps up to the verandah and then a completely different world. The caretaker talked at us for half an hour and charged us nothing beyond what we chose to put in the box.
Charming and genuinely quiet, but it is four rooms, so twenty minutes is more than enough. The person let us in was clearly doing them a favour and we felt the clock ticking.

No sign, no card machine, and the owner just looked up. Two hours passed. If you are the sort of person who wants this city to still have places like it, sit in this room.
Fascinating and I could not do the two steps, so I stood in the shop next door and read through the doorway, which the man found funny. He opens when he opens.

Came without booking on a Saturday and there were spaces. Takes about an hour, the wind does the work, and the verandah has tea. Go before five in summer.

text: Two minute poses, twenty of them, and a tutor who did not explain anything unasked. My drawings are still bad but I understand why now. Booking a week ahead.
Good class, unfair ground. The steps are uneven and I spent most of an hour worrying about my ankles instead of the drawing. Sit on a step and it is fine.

Twelve rupees, and the man who has been on that corner for thirty years puts the box in your hand and points at a bench. Went at seven fifteen and by eight there was nothing left.

The only reason we did not cancel the whole day. He keeps stopping under an awning every two minutes, so you get the rain shots without standing in it. Four weeks of the year it runs.

We got a message at four saying it was cancelled for a downpour, and we went and stood in the arcade instead and it was fine. Fair enough call, and they told us before we left the hotel.
Eighteen people, one piano, and by the second set the drummer was too loud for the room and everyone was shouting over it. Best basement in the city. Four steps down and a queue on Wednesdays.
Could not get in without a booking and the people at the door were not unpleasant about it but they were firm. Ended up at a bar nearby and that was fine too.
Four steps with a handrail on one side only and a dark basement. I did not feel safe and we left. The music was reportedly excellent, which made it worse.
A plywood table, a queue number board from 1961, and a man who does not mind you being there. Twenty minutes went to half an hour. Flat, cool, and completely free.

Three generations of the same family running it and nobody rushed us. The pavak was hot and the cream and jam soda was the best thing I have drunk in a year. The window tables are under an awning so drizzle is fine.
We were four and the window tables were taken, so we waited fifteen minutes standing at the counter, which nobody minded. Good food, small room.
